notes: The author strikes the opening induction on card K and adds On note d’abord que. He records V as the complement of an indexed union of hatted positive Sigma terms and adds an indexed intersection of negative Sigma terms below it. The page writes barred V intersect E_alpha nonempty, then V intersect Sigma_alpha^- nonempty alors que V intersect Sigma_alpha^+ is empty.

After De façon précise, je dis que, the author writes barred V intersect E_alpha = closure of Sigma_alpha^- intersect E_alpha, with qui est donc nonempty and two small lower annotations. He cancels an inverse-inclusion argument involving x and a neighbourhood W, then another formulation in a space whose crossed variable remains Y/Z/X. The live continuation names Y = hatted Sigma_alpha^+ and Z = the union over beta in K minus {alpha} of hatted Sigma_beta^+, calling them fermées and disjointes with separate underlines.

The final written equality is closure(X minus (Y union Z)) intersect Y = closure(X minus Y) intersect Y. The author follows it with ce qui est immédiat. This is an attributed account of the sheet; no proof or mathematical equivalence was checked.

The author’s exact evaluative words are trivial and ce qui est immédiat; the visible draft corrections are preserved. No explicit authorial uncertainty wording is legible. All unsure qualifications in this reader source are editorial.

source_coordinate_convention.graphics: All new paths are manual approximations. Coordinates were transcribed from the displayed image; local source coordinates use the explicit subtraction map and fixed pixel units. No curve-extrema, image-difference or rendered-metric calculation was performed.
source_coordinate_convention.base_west_compensation: For nested graphical nodes, base-west is placed at the declared full-scan left edge of the fixed inner drawing rectangle. Subtracting that rectangle’s local xmin gives the declared inner x origin. node_anchors.json records each exact assignment. The local baseline is anchored at the declared full y; M03 separately states its two-unit left-edge compensation.
